quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is recommended.
Can cause hearing loss.
Is not harmful.
Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Ignore them.
Use your horn and make obscene gestures.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let tailgaters pass. Speeding up makes them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may disregard "No passing zone" markings if the pass was started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must complete the pass within the posted speed limits and within a legal passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass within the posted speed limits and within a legal passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always complete passes within posted speed limits and only in legal passing zones.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle puts you in its blind spot. The driver cannot see you there. You also lose your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When using a motorcycle with which you are unfamiliar, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good riding condition.
Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
Ride as you usually do, since most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times before riding.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding, practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes. Learn the gear pattern first.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as easy to see as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before you slow down or stop so other drivers notice.

questions.question: The only way to rid your body of alcohol is through:

options.text: Time.
Drinking coffee.
Exercising.
Taking a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to occur among:

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Those familiar with their motorcycle.
Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle have the most crashes.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which of these clothing items will NOT reduce crash injuries?

options.text: Heavy shoes
Full-length pants
Shorts
Full-fingered gloves

questions.correctAnswerText: Shorts
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, heavy shoes or boots, full-length pants, a jacket, and full-fingered gloves to reduce injury risk. Use durable materials for the best protection.

questions.question: Space around your motorcycle helps you to:

options.text: React quickly to dangers.
Hide from other drivers.
Avoid being able to escape hazards.
Read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: React quickly to dangers.
questions.explanation: Extra space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to move safely.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: You can see more.
You can see less.
It makes it harder to see past the vehicle.
The other driver can speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see more.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane when preparing to pass. This helps you see better and makes other drivers more aware of you.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide what you plan to do from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you near road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and surface hazards. It discourages drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Which surface does NOT have poor traction?

options.text: Wet pavement
Dry pavement
Lane markings
Snow

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement provides better grip for your tires.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Does not help.
Lets the engine slow you down.
Is illegal.
Should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets the engine slow you down.
questions.explanation: Downshifting smoothly can use the engine to slow your motorcycle. Use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: The body gets rid of almost ______ of alcohol per hour.

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink
questions.explanation: The body removes about one drink of alcohol per hour on average.

questions.question: For protection, motorcycle pants should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Be made of heavy material.
Be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Be short and expose parts of your legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or sturdy synthetic material that cover your entire legs. They should fit snug enough not to flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Let them ride.
Tell them to use empty roads.
Stay out of it.
Take their keys.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take their keys.
questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if needed. Help them find another way home.

questions.question: When riding, goggles:

options.text: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
Protect your face, but not your eyes.
Protect eyes less well than eyeglasses.
Do not protect anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your eyes, but not your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your whole face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute for either one.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic.
A small group can ignore traffic laws to stay together.
Riders will always need to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to keep track of where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Compared to large groups, small groups are easier for other vehicles to pass, less likely to be separated by traffic or lights, and require less rushing from slower riders.

questions.question: When you adjust your rearview mirror, make sure you can see:

options.text: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
Only the lane behind you.
Only the lane next to you.
Most of your helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirror to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. A properly adjusted mirror may show part of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: Motorcycles:

options.text: Do not have blind spots because they are small.
Have blind spots, but they are so small you don't need to worry about them.
Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
Are too small to have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that you should check regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of how you watch the road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Discourage the passenger from wearing protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Do not carry a passenger unless your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. The motorcycle should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear you wear.

questions.question: You should maintain adequate distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Give you time and space to see and react to hazards.
Allow you to tailgate.
Allow traffic counters to count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you enough space to stop or move away if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. Extra space also helps you see hazards on the road, such as potholes.
